scrutinize

/SKROO-tuh-nyz/ - the stress falls on SKROO · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Scrutinize means to examine something closely and critically.

New parents scrutinize every label in the baby aisle, hunting the one ingredient the doctor warned them about.

Example

The failed turbine blade went straight to the metallurgy lab, where investigators scrutinized it for two days — every groove magnified, every discoloration mapped — until a hairline crack no wider than a thread turned up beneath the coating, right where the stress models said to look.

Scrutinize is the right verb because the looking is critical — a hunt for what is wrong, not a general check. Examine would be neutral; inspect suggests a routine pass; scrutinize means every detail is questioned until the flaw has nowhere left to hide.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

examine: Examine is the neutral word for a careful look — a doctor examines a knee, a teacher examines an essay — thorough, but with no suspicion in it. Scrutinize sharpens the same act: the looker is hunting for something wrong and questions every detail until it gives.

vet: To vet is to check a person or plan for hidden problems before approval — the look ends in a yes or a no. Scrutinize carries no gate to pass: you can scrutinize anything, at any point, whenever suspicion demands it. Vetting guards a door; scrutiny hunts a flaw.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

skim: to run the eyes over the surface and no deeper

overlook: to miss what is sitting in plain sight

Where it sits · how thorough and critical the looking gets

glance → inspect → scrutinize → dissect

glance vs. scrutinize: A glance is the weakest look there is — a half-second sweep that registers almost nothing, far milder than scrutinize.

inspect vs. scrutinize: Inspecting goes further than glancing, checking a thing over with real care, but it is still gentler than scrutinize, which hunts for what is wrong.

dissect vs. scrutinize: Dissect goes further than scrutinize: scrutiny questions every detail from the outside, while dissection takes the thing apart piece by piece.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — scrutin: to search through (Latin scrutari, from scruta, ‘rags, trash’)

Suffix — -ize: to make, to treat by

Put it together: Scrutin- (to search through, Latin scrutari) + -ize = to search a thing through and through. The root's own story sets the standard: scrutari originally meant picking through scruta — rags and trash — for anything of value, the most detail-hungry searching there is.

Use the root in a new word: inscrutable: Across three hours of negotiation, her expression stayed perfectly inscrutable.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Scrutinize implies a critical eye hunting for flaws, not just a careful one. Examine is neutral; vet aims at approval; audit is the money-and-records version. When suspicion drives the looking, scrutinize is the word.
